description: Under many parallel runs, hgit commit starves on index.lock; plumbing with a private index and CAS update-ref lands immediately

When many horizon runs are live (13 on 2026-07-29), `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit` can fail for
tens of minutes on `index.lock: File exists` — other runs legitimately hold the shared
index, and a retry loop loses every race. The plumbing route lands on the first attempt:

```bash
export GIT_INDEX_FILE=/tmp/<lane>.index          # private index, no contention
G="git --git-dir=$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR --work-tree=$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE"
$G read-tree HEAD; $G add -- <explicit paths>
TREE=$($G write-tree); P=$($G rev-parse HEAD)
C=$($G commit-tree "$TREE" -p "$P" -F msg.txt)   # add Archon-Run/Session/Task trailers yourself
$G update-ref refs/heads/main "$C" "$P"          # CAS: fails safely if another run advanced HEAD
```

**Why:** the shared index is the contended resource, not the ref. A private `GIT_INDEX_FILE`
sidesteps the lock entirely, and `update-ref` with the expected old value is a
compare-and-swap — if a parallel run committed meanwhile it fails rather than clobbering, and
you re-read HEAD and retry. This also avoids the CAS-arming hazard where staging via the
shared index arms deletions of other lanes' files.

**How to apply:** stage explicit paths only, and supply the provenance trailers manually
since plumbing bypasses the wrapper that stamps them. Verify afterwards with
`merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> HEAD`. Related: [[horizon-commit-gate-needs-thread-reply]].

---
name: piping-lean-to-head-hides-exit-code
description: `lake env lean f.lean | head; echo EXIT=$?` reports head's status, so a failing file looks like EXIT=0
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

`lake env lean File.lean 2>&1 | head -60; echo "EXIT=$?"` prints `EXIT=0` **even when Lean
reported errors** — `$?` is the exit status of `head`, the last command in the pipeline, not
of Lean. On 2026-07-29 this made a 95-minute check on a file with two parse errors look like
a clean pass, and the errors were only visible because they happened to be in the first 60
lines of output.

**Why:** the whole point of the check is the exit code; piping for readability silently
replaces it. Combined with the workspace habit of quoting "kernel EXIT=0" as the verification
claim, this manufactures a false green.

**How to apply:** redirect to a file and echo the status *unpiped*:
`lake env lean F.lean > /tmp/out 2>&1; echo "EXIT=$?"` — then read `/tmp/out`. Or use
`PIPESTATUS[0]` / `set -o pipefail` if a pipe is unavoidable. Always grep the output for
`error` as well as reading the status, and never report EXIT=0 from a piped invocation.
Related: [[gate-quantified-axiom-audit]].
